slot.brief: A diode in series with resistors across a battery; assuming a constant forward voltage drop, find the circuit current.

stem: As shown in the figure, a forward-biased diode has a constant voltage drop of $0.7$ V. Find the total current supplied by the battery.

verdicts.working: The battery’s long plate is at the bottom, so the bottom rail is positive. The diode’s cathode is on the right, making it reverse-biased; in the ideal-diode model, the battery current is zero, which is not listed. If the diode were forward-biased as stated, the equivalent resistance would be 500 Ω + (1 kΩ ∥ 1 kΩ) = 1 kΩ, giving 5.0 mA.
issues: The battery polarity shown makes the diode reverse-biased, contradicting the statement that it is forward-biased. Under the stated forward-bias assumption, option B (5.0 mA) would result, but it does not match the polarity in the figure.

verdicts.working: Effective voltage after diode drop: 5.7 − 0.7 = 5.0 V. Two 1.0 kΩ resistors in parallel give 500 Ω; in series with 500 Ω gives 1000 Ω total. I = 5.0 V / 1000 Ω = 5.0 mA.

working:
$R_{\text{parallel}}=1.0\ \text{k}\Omega\parallel1.0\ \text{k}\Omega=500\ \Omega$
$R_{\text{total}}=500\ \Omega+500\ \Omega=1.0\ \text{k}\Omega$
$I=\dfrac{5.7-0.7}{1.0\times10^3}=5.0\times10^{-3}\ \text{A}=5.0\ \text{mA}$

Independent check: Effective voltage after diode drop: 5.7 − 0.7 = 5.0 V. Two 1.0 kΩ resistors in parallel give 500 Ω; in series with 500 Ω gives 1000 Ω total. I = 5.0 V / 1000 Ω = 5.0 mA.
solution:
The diode drop leaves $5.7-0.7=5.0$ V across the resistor network. The two $1.0\ \text{k}\Omega$ resistors in parallel give $500\ \Omega$, in series with another $500\ \Omega$ resistor:
$$I=\frac{5.0}{500+500}=5.0\times10^{-3}\ \text{A}=5.0\ \text{mA}$$

draft.stem: As shown in the figure, a forward-biased diode has a constant voltage drop of $0.7$ V. Find the total current supplied by the battery.

figure.description: Draw a closed circuit with a $5.7$ V battery on the left, its positive terminal at the top and negative terminal at the bottom. From the positive terminal, draw a wire through a diode oriented for forward current from left to right, then through a $500\ \Omega$ resistor to a junction. From this junction draw two parallel branches, each containing a $1.0\ \text{k}\Omega$ resistor, joining again at a lower junction. Connect the lower junction by wire to the battery's negative terminal. Label the battery voltage and all three resistors. Do not indicate any current value.

draft.distractor_notes: A: gives the current in just one parallel branch. C: ignores the diode's forward voltage drop. D: uses only the series resistor and omits the parallel network's equivalent resistance.
